title: API v2beta behavior flags, deprecation timeline, and migration toolkit
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Summary: We need a resilient deprecation plan for legacy behaviors in the core Redwood API surface (streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs) as we move toward api v2+ defaults. Rather than a hard-cut breaking change, implement a set of server-side behavior flags that preserve legacy semantics, publish a migration guide and SDK helpers, and produce an automated backward-compatibility test suite and dashboards to detect regressions for customers and partners.

Background: Recent runtime improvements and schema-enforcement changes in v2beta tightened streaming chunk semantics and enforced structured-output validation by default. Several top customers rely on previous streaming boundary semantics, permissive JSON outputs, and an older function-calling invocation path. Without a clear migration surface we risk unexpected regressions and customer escalations.

Goals:
- Define behavior flags (server-side and SDK-level toggles) that can be scoped per API key or per-route to preserve legacy behavior for a bounded migration window.
- Publish a comprehensive migration guide with code snippets for JS/Python SDKs and curl examples.
- Deliver an automated backward-compatibility test harness that runs against known customer prompt+tooling fixtures and provides pass/fail signals.
- Implement telemetry and dashboards to track usage of legacy flags, error rates, and generation-delta metrics.
- Run a staged deprecation: announce -> opt-in grace window -> forced opt-out with final sunset date.

Scope: Streaming chunk semantics, function/tool-calling call and response envelope shapes, structured-output enforcement (JSON schema validation), behavior of partial responses and failure modes. This ticket coordinates PM deliverables: migration guide, comms schedule, acceptance criteria, and customer-facing examples. Engineering tickets (ENG-9123, ENG-9180) cover runtime flag implementation and SDK support.

Non-goals: Changes to model weights, quantization, or Dedicated capacity autoscaling. Not addressing embedding output format in this ticket (follow-up).

Deliverables:
- Migration doc (Confluence) with 1-page executive summary + deep-dive code samples for streaming, function calling, and structured outputs.
- Behavior flag spec (server flag names, default states, per-key/per-route scopes).
- SDK patches (JS & Python) exposing client-side convenience wrappers to set flags and surface warnings.
- Backward-compatibility test harness (GitHub repo) with example customer fixtures.
- Observability dashboard (Console tile) tracking legacy-flag adoption, regression count, and customer opt-in rates.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field for discrete items.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior flags documented and named: legacy_streaming_semantics, permissive_structured_output, legacy_tool_envelope
Runtime support: server accepts flags scoped to API keys and route configs (ENG implements per-key/per-route enforcement)
SDK support: JS and Python clients expose setBehaviorFlags(options) and emit a deprecation warning when legacy flags are used
Migration guide published with at least three end-to-end examples: streaming->chunks, function-calling migration, structured-output schema adjustments
Automated compatibility test harness able to run a suite of 50 representative prompts and report pass/fail and diffs
Observability: new dashboard shows legacy-flag usage by customer, error/rejection rate delta, and time-to-first-failure for migrated clients
Customer communication plan drafted and approved (email + in-console banner + changelog) with minimum 90 days opt-in window
comments: 2025-02-21: Kickoff w/ Eng (Mateo Alvarez) and DevEx (Lena Cho). Eng asked for per-route scoping — accepted; added dependencies ENG-9123 and ENG-9180.
2025-02-24: Design review — suggested in-console microcopy for behavior flag warnings; flagged for UX review with DES-204 next cycle.
2025-02-26: Engineering spike completed (ENG-9123) — server flag prototype exists, needs auth-scoping and performance benching.
2025-03-01: Draft migration guide uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/API/API+v2beta+Migration+Guide (internal). Feedback requested from runtime team.
2025-03-03: Scope refinement: exclude embeddings format changes from this rollout to reduce blast radius. Updated acceptance criteria accordingly.
2025-03-05: PR opened for SDK helpers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 — includes setBehaviorFlags and console warning surfaces. Not ready for merge; awaits tests and UX copy.
Next steps: finalize flag naming (deadline 2025-03-12), complete compatibility harness integration, schedule customer beta invites for 2025-04-07.
testing_plan: Unit tests for server-side flag parsing and enforcement (ENG), coverage >= 90% on the flag codepaths
Integration tests: run compatibility harness against latest runtime in preprod; record generation diffs for streaming and function-calling
End-to-end customer fixtures: collect 10 high-priority customer prompts and run weekly regression checks during migration window
Canary rollout: internal canary -> invited customers -> general opt-in -> forced sunset with 30-day final warning
Post-deprecation validation: run compatibility harness against production defaults and publish regression report
rollout_plan: 1) Announcement + docs (Day 0). 2) Behavior flags enabled by default for legacy keys (opt-out) for 90 days. 3) Open opt-in program for customers to test default v2 behaviors in a sandbox (Day 30+). 4) After 90-day grace, new keys default to v2 behaviors; legacy keys can still opt-in via behavior flags for 6 more months. 5) Final sunset notice 30 days before flag removal. Communication channels: email to billing & admin contacts, in-console banner, changelog entry, and support playbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers may not discover per-key flags and experience silent regressions. Mitigation: in-console banner + API warning header + usage alert to admins.
Risk: SDK changes cause extra latency or unexpected errors. Mitigation: SDK PR gated behind integration tests and staged release to npm/PyPI canary channels.
Risk: Compatibility harness misses edge-case prompts. Mitigation: partner with Solutions Eng to onboard 5 customers with custom fixtures early in the beta.
Risk: Observability gaps for structured-output rejections. Mitigation: add explicit rejection/validation metrics and trace ids in logs for quick triage.
